answer: The answer is committed as a 329 bit hash at open and revealed at close, and a reveal that does not match the commitment is void. Because the inlet commitment is timestamped in the atlas ledger, the dawn audit verifies the pair and a late swap fails the hash. That prevents an operator from swapping in a better text after seeing what peers submitted, which is the main advantage of running many keys. Each impostor pays 13 dollars up front. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
